subject: OrchidBank: elevated 5xxs & reserved-QPS shortfall — request for exec alignment
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@orchidbank.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production impact — spikes in errors and throughput gap

David / team,

We're seeing a sustained spike in 5xx errors starting around 09:50 UTC this morning (~2 hours ago). Token throughput from our production integration is ~28% below our committed reserved QPS despite requests ingesting at the expected rate. Latency is up across the board for our high-priority routes and we've had 3 customer-facing failures so far (attached sample rows).

Key points: 
- 5xx rate peaked at 4.9% for the last 15m (normally <0.2%).
- Our telemetry shows queueing and token throttles on requests routed to our reserved pool (account: ORCHID-63).
- We have a Friday cutover planned next week; this impacts our ability to complete smoke tests.

Please advise immediate mitigations and whether this is a capacity/reservation problem on your end. We need an ETA for a fix and whether you can provision burst capacity while we evaluate.

Attachments: orchid_errors_sample.csv

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Operations, OrchidBank
ops@orchidbank.com
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — spikes in errors and throughput gap

Samir — thanks for the heads up (looping in infra/telemetry). We're triaging now.

Immediate ask from our side: can you confirm whether Orchid is routing any new model variants this morning or increased batch sizes from your side? That helps rule in/out a client-side change.

Karthik / infra: please check dedicated pool "redwood-dedicated-usw2-07" for saturation, queue depth, and model variant substitution anomalies. Report back with the top failure classes and any mitigation you can push fast (routing fallback, canary to hosted, temporary burst). 

I'll coordinate with Marissa on the customer comms and escalation path if we need to offer credits or an SLA exception.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — spikes in errors and throughput gap

Quick technical summary from infra: 
- Observed behavior: dedicated pool redwood-dedicated-usw2-07 reached sustained GPU util ceiling ~99% on nodes serving OrchidBank routes starting 09:42 UTC. Concurrently we saw KV cache churn and elevated context-switching inside the runtime. This aligns with elevated token latencies and queueing.
- Root cause hypothesis: Orchid's prod traffic started hitting a larger model variant (v3.1-large-ops) due to a mis-tagged route in their canary config. The larger model increases per-token compute by ~2.1x which explains the reserved-QPS shortfall.
- Immediate mitigations we can push (minutes -> hours):
   1) Forced routing: move Orchid traffic to v3.1-medium-ops variant for next 24h (low-risk, minimal quality delta).
   2) Enable focused burst: add +30% burst capacity to the dedicated pool for 3 hours from now (requires exec approval for quota overcommit).
   3) Apply hotfix to better throttle batched requests at the edge (reduces KV thrash).

Attached: grafana_pool_20260914.png (utilization graph), orchid_errors_sample.csv (extracted 5xx rows).

I'll start the forced routing plan if we get alignment from Sales/Customer success and the go-ahead on a short burst. Also creating JIRA HZ-4123 to track the remediation playbook.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal <legal@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — spikes in errors and throughput gap

Team — this is an exec-level customer impact. Orchids is on an annual reserved contract (DEAL-03847) and the cutover next week makes this time-sensitive. Priorities:
1) Authorize the +30% burst for a 3 hour window now (we can decide billing/credits after stabilization).
2) Push the routing fallback to v3.1-medium-ops immediately and validate error rate reduction in the first 15m.
3) Schedule customer sync in next 30 minutes to confirm we've triaged and set expectations.

Rishi — can you OK a one-time SLA exception/commitment credit if we fail to meet the agreed SLOs this week? Legal, please stand by for temporary SLA amendment language if needed. Priyom — please coordinate the customer-facing note and calendar invite.

Samir — thanks for flagging and for the patience. Quick update and next steps: 

1) We've forced-routed Orchid traffic to v3.1-medium-ops at 10:45 UTC; infra reports an immediate drop in 5xxs from ~4.9% to ~0.4% over the next 12 minutes. See the attached stabilization snapshot (we've also uploaded to the shared drive).
2) Rishi approved a one-time +30% burst for 3 hours to buy headroom while we fully validate.
3) We opened JIRA HZ-4123 to track the post-mortem and configuration cleanup.
4) Action items: 
   - Redwood infra to deliver a post-mortem and fix the routing mis-tag by EOW (owner: Karthik).
   - Sales/legal to confirm any credit posture or SLA amendment (owner: Marissa).
   - Ops at Orchid to confirm whether any client-side routing/batch changes were triggered; this will help prevent recurrence.

I've scheduled a 30-min sync at 12:00 UTC today (calendar invite sent). HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/OrchidBank. JIRA: HZ-4123.

We'll monitor closely and follow up after the post-mortem.

Best,
Priyom
